subject: "Incorrect" pooled detection function from the Minke example

messages.author: 54c94f7c2bf78491
messages.subject: "Incorrect" pooled detection function from the Minke example
parts:
Hello,

Reading through this example:

http://distancesampling.org/R/vignettes/minke.html

... the final summary states:

Pooled detection function

Estimates of group abundance when a detection function is fitted to data pooled across strata. These results are actually incorrect because effort was not equally allocated between the strata. The southern stratum is much smaller (84000km2) than the northern (630000km2). But the southern stratum is more desirable habitat for the minke whales because it is closer to the ice edge in Antarctica. The southern stratum had much greater survey effort per area than the northern stratum. This is not represented in the pooled analysis.


If I understand correctly, the results are incorrect because the detection function will be biased towards fitting the data from the stratum with more observations, at the expense of fit to the less-observations stratum. The density estimate for the two areas would be affected, so despite accounting for the area when multiplying up from the density estimate (and despite the density estimate accounting for survey effort), the abundance estimates would be wrong.


Am I right in thinking this is only the case when the detection function is different between strata? If we imagine a case where the detectability is identical between two strata, and thus the detection function is identical if fitted separately or pooled, this would not affect the density estimates, even if the area and effort is different? (Of course, the abundance estimate would differ if the area differed).


A real world example of this might be pooling temporally rather than spatially - combining data with a low n from the same time period in multiple years to improve the detection function, if it is assumed that detectability has not changed between years.

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: {Suspected Spam} [distance-sampling] "Incorrect" pooled detection function from the Minke example
parts:
Olly

The heart of the issue hinted at in the minke whale vignette is unequal allocation of effort among strata and how this interacts with the property of pooling robustness.

Look at this summary of the minke data (available from `summary(ds-object)`)

Summary statistics:
  Region   Area CoveredArea  Effort  n  k         ER      se.ER     cv.ER
1  North 630582     4075.14 1358.38 49 12 0.03607238 0.01317937 0.3653591
2  South  84734     1453.23  484.41 39 13 0.08051031 0.01809954 0.2248102
3  Total 715316     5528.37 1842.79 88 25 0.04775368 0.01129627 0.2365529

The northern stratum is larger (by a factor of ~7) and has roughly x4 times the sampling effort as the southern stratum.  For that x4 sampling effort the number of detections is only x1.25. 

The quantity of interest is proportion of each stratum receiving effort (CoveredArea/Area by stratum).  That ratio is 0.0065 for the North and 0.0171 for the South.  This is the unequal allocation of effort--the South having proportionally greater effort (2% of the South was samples while 0.6% of the North).

This unequal effort allocation between strata results in the breakdown of pooling robustness that ordinarily applies in distance sampling whereby the overall density estimate is unbiased even if sources of heterogeneity in detectability are not taken into account.

More directly to your question, will this be a problem if the detection function in the two strata are identical: no.  Because there is no heterogeneity in detectability, so you're not asking anything of pooling robustness.
